summary.headline: Jash Engineering FY26 consolidated revenue rose only 1% to INR757 crore; FY27 guidance is INR875 crore at 12-13% PAT margin.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated income was INR757 crore versus INR746 crore, with management calling the growth disappointing. US tariff volatility (25% in January, 50% in June) led to slower US production, and the Middle East war disrupted Middle East deliveries and shipping to Far East and Southeast Asia. Domestic business grew 18% and held margins, so standalone PAT margin fell only from 14.38% to 13.38%. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR875 crore against an order book of INR899 crore (as on 1 May) and about INR45 crore already billed.

financial_highlights.change: vs 14.39% in FY25 and 14.21% in FY24 (management quoted 14.38% for prior year in opening remarks)
INR827 crore at end-March per BSE monthly data cited by analyst; INR627 crore export, INR272 crore India

financial_highlights.value: INR67 crore total (INR37 crore plant and machinery, INR30 crore acquisitions)
Includes about INR10 crore one-off US bank charge
INR9 crore vs about INR3 crore normal

segments.name: Waterfront Fluid Controls (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue guided to about INR60 crore, 75-85% of last year; UK AMP cycle slowdown delayed growth, with GBP5.5-6 million (about INR65-70 crore) projected and strong growth expected from H2. Penstocks UK acquisition completed early April, to merge with Waterfront.

segments.name: Rodney Hunt (US)
segments.commentary: Order book about USD38-39 million; FY26 revenue around USD30 million, FY27 target USD38 million, more than 25% growth on last year. New Houston plant and Saudi plant targeted for commissioning by December 2027.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Water control gates are the largest product line, followed by screens and valves (valves rose to 13% of mix from 11%); hydro power, pumping and other about 8%. Mix shift away from Far East (16% to 10%) noted by analyst.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Management cites about 44.5% of business in India and about 55% outside India. US was about 45% of revenue per analyst.

segments.name: WestTech / Jash Process Equipment
segments.commentary: Acquired mid-January 2026; contributes a small share of FY26 revenue. Guided to about INR40 crore in FY27 (analyst reading); outsourced manufacturing to be moved into Jash plants to cut costs.

segments.name: Shivpad (India)
segments.commentary: Merged into Jash Engineering; Q4 quality and labour issues described as largely resolved after retraining team at Indore; no incremental capacity added.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target INR875 crore, backed by INR899 crore order book and about INR45 crore billed as of early May; INR28 crore negotiated and INR80 crore under negotiation.
FY27 PAT margin guided at 12-13%; gross margin guided at 50-55%.

Five-year target to double revenue from INR757 crore to above INR1,500 crore; capacity of about INR1,200 crore on 2-3 shifts with current Indian plants, rising above INR1,500 crore once Houston and Saudi plants are online.
Rodney Hunt USD target: USD75 million in five years, from about USD30 million today.
Q4 gross margin gain attributed to forex (billing at about INR92/USD against INR82 estimate); management says it lasts while the dollar stays high.
FY27 capex planned at about INR15-16 crore for the five Indian plants; US and Saudi capex not yet quantified.
Singapore sea-level projects: offers of about USD800-900 million submitted; first orders possibly from 2029, awards from 2028.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR67 crore: INR37 crore plant and machinery and INR30 crore acquisitions.
FY27 Indian plant capex about INR15-16 crore across five plants.

Rodney Hunt Houston plant: land and drawings approved, but cost quotes have risen to USD7-8.5 million versus USD4.2 million placed earlier; prior contractor closed down. Commissioning target December 2027.
Saudi Arabia plant: company set up, land not yet acquired; site visit planned end-June/July 2026; commissioning target December 2027 (earlier December 2026).
Rodney Hunt Orange (Massachusetts) constrained by production staff shortage; new capacity chosen in Houston.
demand_pricing: US tariff: management says stability matters more than level; 25% to 50% increase mid-year led to under-estimated costs on January-June orders. Section 232 shift cited as continuing uncertainty.
Export order book about INR627 crore; over 75% of export order in hand expected to benefit from forex gains.
Hong Kong Yuen Long Barrage project about INR40 crore (including small gates and valves); Chennai desalination project (VA Tech) over INR35 crore; Saudi Al Haer sewage treatment project in progress.
Middle East deliveries still blocked; order intake continues in Southeast Asia, Middle East, Far East and Europe.
Raw material prices rising: about 20% rise in India raw material cost per CFO; US steel also more expensive.

qa_highlights.question: Is domestic revenue flat in FY27 given INR327 crore FY26 base versus INR320 crore projected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the mix is balanced by choice; domestic margins are higher because low-margin domestic jobs are not taken. Domestic may rise if exports fall short.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 gross margin improvement only forex or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex-driven: orders quoted at INR82/USD and billed at about INR92 gain INR10 per dollar. Gross margin guided at 50-55% for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative given WestTech and carry-over?
qa_highlights.answer: Management calls it conservative given WestTech integration and the US tariff history; it expects growth of 13-17% and margin of at least 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt capacity and growth after Houston and Saudi plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Target USD75 million in five years; USD100 million not planned. Plant costs rose sharply, and US hiring constraints shaped the Houston decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is open to opportunities that are small and scalable; it is merging subsidiaries of similar businesses to reduce their number.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Singapore sea-level opportunity size INR5,000-6,000 crore and when does it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Clarified as offers of USD800-900 million, not an order; awards start 2028, first orders 2029, spread over 20-25 years; market share targeted 20-40%.

risks_watch: US tariff regime changes (Section 232 shift) and steel input cost inflation affecting project margins.
Middle East war delaying dispatches; Saudi plant land acquisition and commissioning timeline (December 2027) at risk.
Rodney Hunt Houston plant cost overrun (USD4.2 million to USD7-8.5 million) and hiring constraints in Orange, Massachusetts.
Other expenses inflated by one-off bank charge; overheads growing 7-10% against low revenue growth.
Forex-driven margin gain may reverse if the dollar falls; order book conversion and Q1 billing (INR36 crore overflow from March).
WestTech and Penstocks integration; margin outlook at WestTech not yet guided.
summary.management_tone: Candid and conservative on guidance, while confident on the order book and domestic business. Management is cautious on US expansion and attributes the weak year mainly to tariff and war disruption.
key_quotes: If it is 50%, we are happy with that 50% . However, it should continue at that , variation results into our estimating at lower tariff, and then when the higher tariff comes into play, it results into losses for us
So, I would rather remain conservative and try to achieve whatever I say rather than being too optimistic and then failing again and again.
Order flow will not get impacted, if you need water, you need water.

Saudi Arabia plant (land not yet acquired), commissioning target December 2027

growth.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR875 crore vs INR757 crore in FY26 (about 16% growth), backed by a INR899 crore order book as of 1 May and about INR45 crore billed; the Houston and Saudi plants are not commissioning until December 2027, so near-term growth rests on the order book.
